title: Out of the Axis
summary:
Infantile postural asymmetry is the 4th most common newborn problem from the perspective of physiotherapists (Riedel, 2009). Whether the use of a Goal Attainment Scale (GAS) for structured treatment guidance of parents improves the therapeutic success of physiotherapy according to Vojta in children with infantile postural asymmetry is to be investigated.
The GAS as a goal achievement scale is a standardized instrument with which individual goals can be defined together with patients and thus involve them more closely in the treatment process. (Gordon & Rockwood, 1999)
The dissertation answers the question: "Can the use of a GAS for structured treatment guidance of parents improve the therapeutic success of physiotherapy according to Vojta in children with infantile postural asymmetry". 
The research question is: "Does structured, topic-related goal setting together with parents lead to more effective treatment of infantile postural asymmetry in their children?" 
Within the research question, an intervention group and a control group will be used to test whether the use of GAS can improve the recovery of infants with infantile postural asymmetry towards symmetry over a period of 8 weeks. 
In this randomized intervention study, the Vaclav Vojta method is applied to the subjects of both study groups (Vojta, 2000). The intervention group also receives GAS to accompany the therapy at home. The goals are reformulated every 14 days and documented over the course of the therapy using a therapy protocol. For the pre/post comparison of the therapy effect, Philippi's asymmetry scale is used by means of video analysis and the videos are evaluated by three blinded assessors (Philippi et al., 2007). The plan is to randomize 60 infants with infantile postural asymmetry and their parents into two study arms. An intervention group and a control group. The intervention group will receive GAS to support the intervention, the control group will not receive GAS. All infants in both groups will receive the same therapy twice a week by the researcher and daily therapy at home by the parents.
conditions: Other congenital deformities of skull, face and jaw

interventions.name:
Clinical and structural parameters:
The clinical and structural parameters are measured using the Philippi score, which records the documented data. At the end of the study, the differences in the average change in the severity of the clinical picture between the two groups are measured.

A control group in which the infants are also treated according to Vojta (see detailed description arm 1), without the use of GAS.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Infantile postural asymmetry, head misalignment, infantile scoliosis
Exclusion criteria:
Severe neurological diseases, damage or malfunction of the nervous system, e.g. neuromuscular disease
